newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DETROIT ADVANCES, DALLAS, ANAHEIM, BUFFALO GOING TO GAME 7.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DETROIT ADVANCES, DALLAS, ANAHEIM, BUFFALO GOING TO GAME 7.

text.p: Back-up goalie Steve Shields stopped 31 shots for his first career shutout as the Buffalo Sabres forced a decisive seventh game in their NHL Eastern Conference playoff series by blanking the Ottawa Senators 3-0.

Shields, making his third straight start in place of the injured Dominik Hasek, never gave the boisterous Corel Centre crowd reason to cheer as Buffalo tied the best-of-seven, first-round series at three games apiece.
Buffalo took the lead on Brian Holzinger's goal early in the first period and retreated into a defensive shell much of the rest of the way.
"Steve Shields was a wall in there tonight," said Sabres coach Ted Nolan. "He's a character guy with a lot of confidence in himself. And tonight he did the job for us."

Also staving off elimination to knot their respective best-of-seven Western Conference series at three games apiece were the Dallas Stars and the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim, who also accomplished the feat on the road.

One team advanced as the Detroit Red Wings beat the St Louis Blues 3-1 to win their Western series four games to two. The Red Wings also triumphed over the home team, making it a clean sweep for the NHL's road warriors on Sunday.
Sabres coach Nolan, despite missing star goalie Hasek, who is nursing a sprained knee, had vowed that the series would return to Buffalo.
"I had a tremendous amount of confidence in this team," said Nolan, whose team will host Game Seven on Tuesday.
Alexei Zhitnik and Jason Dawe had the Sabres' other goals.
Ottawa went 0-for-6 with the man advantage after recording six power-play goals in the first five games of the series.
"If you talk about the result, I guess it was my best outing," said Shields.
Despite Shields's heroics, Hasek will play in Game Seven if he is able, Nolan said. "There's only one Dominik. He led us to where we are, so if he's ready, he's our guy."

In St Louis, Brendan Shanahan's power-play goal 67 seconds into the second period snapped a 1-1 tie and propelled the Detroit Red Wings to a 3-1 win that eliminated the Blues from the Stanley Cup playoffs.
Vyacheslav Kozlov and Kirk Maltby also scored for the Red Wings, who ousted St Louis for the second year in a row.
Mike Vernon stopped 24 shots for Detroit in earning his 61st career playoff victory.
Brett Hull accounted for the St. Louis offence, staking the Blues to a 1-0 lead 2:12 into the contest.

The Red Wings' "Russian Unit" tied the game on the power play with 11:15 left in the first period. Igor Larionov dug the puck out of the right corner and gave it to Sergei Fedorov at the point. Fedorov slid a pass to Kozlov, who zipped a quick, low shot that went between Fuhr's pads.

After Shanahan slammed home a rebound to give Detroit the lead, St Louis had an apparent tying goal disallowed in the second period when video replays showed Pierre Turgeon's left skate was in the crease before he slid a rebound under Vernon in the final minute of the second period.
Maltby scored an insurance goal with 11:36 to play.
In Edmonton, Mike Modano scored with 5:18 left to break a tie as the Dallas Stars forced a decisive seventh game with a 3-2 victory over the Edmonton Oilers in their series.
Dallas will host Game Seven on Tuesday. The Stars, who won the Central Division, had the best road record in the NHL this season and posted their second win of the series in Edmonton.

"I haven't been around this level for very long, but this is the best hockey I've ever been involved with," Dallas coach Ken Hitchcock said. "It's been a hell of a series and if they put it in a boxed set and sell it, I'll buy a copy."

With the teams playing four skaters a side, Modano gained the puck in the right corner, went behind the net and skated around the perimeter before going into the slot, where his wrist shot went off the stick of Edmonton's Ryan Smyth and into the bottom right corner of the net past Curtis Joseph.
Modano has four goals in the series.
Andy Moog finished 33 saves and Joseph had 38.
"The fact that the road team has won four of the first six games shows how hard both teams are working," said Moog.
In Phoenix, Paul Kariya scored his second goal of the game at 7:29 of overtime and the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim forced a seventh game in their series with a 3-2 win over the Coyotes.

Teemu Selanne flipped the puck from his own zone across the Phoenix blue line, where it hopped over the stick of Coyotes defenceman Gerald Diduck. Kariya picked it up and wristed a shot from the left faceoff circle that beat Nikolai Khabibulin high to the stick side.
"We got lucky in overtime, but I thought we deserved to win the game in regulation. We didn't," Ducks coach Ron Wilson said. "In the end, I've heard that justice prevails."
Anaheim will host Game Seven on Tuesday.
The Ducks squandered a two-goal lead in the third period as Phoenix, who had won the last three games in the series, forced overtime on goals by Darrin Shannon and Keith Tkachuk.
Khabibulin made 36 saves for the Coyotes, who were outshot 39-21.
